item.title: Incarico post-doc: Research on religious freedom in prison (special regimes, pluralism, female detention) and integrative teaching of Canon and Ecclesiastical Law. (ROMA "La Sapienza")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-07 23:59
Institution: ROMA "La Sapienza", Rome
Field: Law / 12/GIUR-07 Diritto e religione

The ideal candidate must have proven research experience in the field of religious freedom law, with particular reference to its protection within the prison system and its balancing with order and security requirements. Professional and scientific research experience regarding the protection of religious freedom in detention is required, with a specific focus on special prison regimes and female detention. Qualifying elements include the aforementioned professional experience and participation in research projects on religious freedom in prison, pluralism, and vulnerability.

item.title: Contratto di ricerca: The Legitimacy of Democratic Systems: The Role of Social Rights (ROMA "La Sapienza")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-07 23:59
Institution: ROMA "La Sapienza", Rome
Field: Law / 12/GIUR-05 Diritto costituzionale e pubblico

Contemporary democratic systems are experiencing a period of severe delegitimation, alongside strong signs of weakness in constitutional frameworks and the principles of the rule of law. Within this context of legal uncertainty, a major divisive factor is represented by citizens' dissatisfaction with institutions, particularly regarding the need for equality of treatment and the guarantee of social rights. Based on these elements, the research must therefore direct its investigation towards the remaining leeway for public and budgetary policies within the EMU framework, also aiming to identify legal competences and functions related to the balanced financial coverage of the essential…

item.title: Incarico post-doc: Incarico Post-Doc - GIUR-14/A - Restorative Justice in the Regional Context of Friuli Venezia Giulia: Critical Issues and Prospects Based on Legal Practice Experience (Univ. TRIESTE)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-16 23:59
Institution: Univ. TRIESTE, Trieste
Field: Law / 12/GIUR-14 Diritto penale

This research project addresses the implementation of restorative justice within the Italian legal system, with particular attention to the regional context of Friuli Venezia Giulia. Building on a systematic and critical reconstruction of the framework introduced by Legislative Decree No. 150/2022 – in its substantive, procedural, and organizational dimensions – the research extends to an empirical field investigation, conducted through semi-structured interviews with criminal defense lawyers and judges operating in the region. This empirical activity will take place in part at the Camera Penale di Trieste for an expected period of four months, during which tutoring will be provided by the…

item.title: Incarico post-doc: Commercial Law in the Papal States of the Restoration: The Provisional Regulation of 1821 Between the Napoleonic Legacy and the ius commune (ROMA "La Sapienza")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-02 23:59
Institution: ROMA "La Sapienza", Roma
Field: Law / 12/GIUR-16 Storia del diritto medievale e moderno

This research will analyze papal commercial law during the Restoration era, examining the impact of Napoleonic legislation on common law beginning with the 1821 Regulation. The study will examine the debate on commercial jurisdiction, codification projects, and university teaching in Rome. Based on archival sources and contemporary legal scholarship, the study aims to chart the comparison between the “mos italicus” and the French school. The ultimate goal is a comprehensive reconstruction of the system, complete with a bibliography of sources and scholarly publications

Field: Law / 12/GIUR-15 Diritto romano e fondamenti del diritto europeo

The research aims to study Roman imperial legislation during the early Principate, and in particular the body of constitutions issued during the period spanning the reigns of Augustus and Nerva (27 BC–98 AD). These texts are of fundamental importance not only to historians of Roman law, but also to philologists, archaeologists and historians of classical culture
